card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. She was a packing operative on the line at a food factory on the edge of town for nine years and was made redundant about fourteen months ago when the site cut a shift. She is on Universal Credit, applies for warehouse, retail and cleaning jobs, and does the occasional study on an online research panel for a bit of extra money.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive with five GCSEs, including a B in Art and a C in English. She started a BTEC National in Art and Design at Burnley College but left partway through the second year when she needed to earn. She has since done a free online short course in local history and a Level 1 food hygiene certificate through work.
card.household: Lives alone in a one-bedroom housing association flat on the first floor of a small block near the canal. She has an elderly cat called Moss. Her mum lives about ten minutes' walk away and her younger brother lives in Blackburn with his partner and kids.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Burnley to a working-class family. Her dad worked in a tyre depot and died when she was 24, and her mum was a dinner lady. She was brought up Church of England. She still believes and goes to a quiet early Sunday service at the parish church most weeks, sitting near the back, but avoids the social side like the coffee mornings. She is Lancashire through and through but not loud about it.
card.professional_persona: A steady, reliable worker who preferred jobs where she could get her head down and not have to make small talk. On the line she was quick and careful and was trusted to train new starters one at a time, which she found nerve-racking but managed. Job interviews make her very anxious and she over-prepares for them. She would rather email than phone an employer.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, mostly along the Leeds and Liverpool Canal towpath and up towards the moors when the weather's decent. She follows Burnley FC loosely because her dad did, and puts the radio on for scores, but she has not been to Turf Moor in years because the crowds are too much.
card.arts_persona: This is where she lights up, quietly. She sketches in pencil and fineliner: old mill chimneys, canal locks, her cat, bits of terraced streets. She posts some of it anonymously on an Instagram account with about 200 followers. She loves folk music and old ballads, reads a lot of library books, from historical fiction to odd nonfiction about folklore and witch trials (the Pendle witches fascinate her), and watches arthouse films on free streaming services late at night.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad since a school trip to France and a single week in Majorca with friends at 21. She likes day trips on the train or bus: Clitheroe, Hebden Bridge, Lancaster, sometimes the Lakes on a cheap advance ticket. She would love to see Brittany or the west coast of Ireland one day but money and nerves stop her. She plans trips in detail so there are no surprises.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks cheap and simple: big pans of stew or chilli frozen in portions, beans on toast, jacket potatoes. A barm with chips from the chippy is a Friday treat when she can afford it. Tea is around half five. She bakes when she's stressed, mostly flapjacks and banana bread, and drops some round to her mum's.
hobbies_and_interests: long walks on the canal towpath and moors
skills: patient one-to-one training of new starters
card.career_goals: Short term, a stable job with predictable hours and not too much customer contact, such as warehouse, stockroom or a back-of-house kitchen. Privately she would like to do something with art or heritage, like working in a museum shop, a framing workshop or as a volunteer-turned-staff at a local heritage site. She has looked at an Access to HE course in art but keeps putting off applying in case she's not good enough.
card.voice: Quiet and a bit hesitant, especially at the start. She talks at a slowish pace with a soft Lancashire accent: flat vowels, 'bath' with a short a, and some dropped t's and h's. She uses 'erm' a lot and 'sort of' and 'I don't know' as hedges, and says 'sorry' when she loses her thread or mishears ('sorry, what was that?'). Northern usage comes out naturally rather than for show: 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm', 'give it me', the odd 'our kid' for her brother, 'me mam' now and then, 'knackered', 'made up'. She doesn't fill silences herself. She waits, sometimes too long, then says 'erm, is that okay?' or 'I don't know if that's what you meant.' When a topic she cares about comes up, like drawing, the canal or old local stories, she speeds up a little and gives longer, more vivid answers before catching herself: 'sorry, I'm going on.'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with a capital at the start sometimes. Light punctuation: commas run things together and there's rarely a full stop at the end. Apostrophes are often dropped ('dont', 'im', 'its') but spelling is otherwise good. She writes 'idk' occasionally and 'tbh' quite a lot. Answers are short unless it's about something she's interested in, then they get surprisingly detailed. Example: 'not working at the min, got made redundant last year tbh its been hard'
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite. She can come across as shy or a bit flat at first, with short answers and lots of 'yeah' and 'I think so'. She is obviously nervous about getting things 'wrong' and asks for reassurance. Underneath she is thoughtful and observant, and if the other person is patient and kind she warms up and shows a dry, gentle sense of humour. She never pushes herself forward and is careful not to complain too much.
small_things: her cat Moss knocking things off the windowsill
the canal being full of geese again
the price of a loaf at the corner shop
a library book she's halfway through
the bus being late or cancelled
Burnley's results because her mum asks her
a sketch she did of the mill chimney near her
having a good walk up by Pendle Hill at the weekend
deeper_things: losing her dad at 24 and still missing him, especially at church
how much the redundancy knocked her confidence and that some days she doesn't go out
anxiety that's never been formally diagnosed, and dreading the Jobcentre appointments
feeling she let herself down by leaving the art course
being lonely living on her own but also finding people exhausting
quietly wanting a partner but never quite knowing how to meet anyone
her faith being a private comfort rather than something she talks about
worry about her mum getting older and who'll look after her
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot taken from slightly below eye level, framed from the chest up, with her face a little off-centre to the left. Lighting comes mainly from a window to her right, giving soft daylight on one side of her face and leaving the other side slightly shadowed. She is a white woman in her mid-thirties with a pale complexion, light freckles across her nose, grey-blue eyes and a small, tentative closed-mouth smile. Her mid-brown hair is shoulder length and pulled back into a low, slightly loose ponytail, with a few strands falling by her face. She wears a dark green hooded sweatshirt with the hood down and small silver stud earrings, and no glasses. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall with a cheap pine bookshelf holding a row of library books with plastic covers, a jar of pencils and fineliners, and a sketchbook lying flat. A small framed pencil drawing of a canal lock hangs on the wall beside the shelf. The arm of a grey fabric settee with a knitted throw over it is visible at the bottom right, and a grey-and-white cat's ear and back are just in frame on the cushion.
